title: The river didn’t open first.
paragraphs:
The river didn’t open first.
Faith stepped first.
Picture the moment.

The Jordan River was not calm that day. Scripture tells us it was flood season — the river overflowing its banks (Joshua 3:15). The water was wild, loud, dangerous. One wrong step and a man could be swept away.
And God looked at Israel and said something that sounded almost unreasonable:
“Step in.”

Not after the water moves.
Not when it feels safe.
Not when the path is visible.
Step now.
Joshua told the people:
“Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you.” — Joshua 3:5
Notice the order.

Not wonders first.
Consecration first.

Not miracles first.
Surrender first.
This is where many of us pause.
Because we love the idea of God doing wonders. We post about miracles. We pray for breakthroughs. We sing songs about the promised land.
But very few people talk about the moment before the miracle.
The moment when the river is still raging.
The moment when God asks for obedience that feels terrifying.

The priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant walked toward the water. The Ark represented the presence of the living God among His people. It went first because Israel’s confidence was never supposed to be in strategy, strength, or numbers.
Their confidence was God Himself.
Joshua declared:
“By this you shall know that the living God is among you…” — Joshua 3:10
Among you.

Not distant.
Not silent.
Not indifferent.
Among.
But here’s the part that grips the heart.
The water did not stop immediately.
Scripture says:
“When the soles of the feet of the priests bearing the ark of the LORD… shall rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters… shall be cut off.” — Joshua 3:13
Did you see that?
Their feet had to touch the flood.

They had to feel the cold water.
They had to sense the current pushing.
They had to step where logic said don’t step.
And the moment their feet touched the water…
The river stopped.
The waters upstream rose up in a heap, and the people of Israel crossed on dry ground (Joshua 3:16–17).
Let that sink in.
God did not remove the obstacle first.
He invited them to trust Him in the presence of the obstacle.
That is the tension of faith.

Faith is not pretending the river isn’t dangerous.
Faith is stepping because God is faithful.
Some of you reading this know exactly what your Jordan looks like.

For some, it’s a marriage on the edge.
For others, it’s a secret addiction nobody knows about.
For someone else, it’s fear about the future.
Maybe God has been whispering something to your heart:

Forgive them.
Let go.
Confess.
Start the calling.
Step out.
Trust Me.
But the river is loud.
And we keep waiting for God to calm the water first.
Joshua 3 reminds us that sometimes the miracle happens after the step of obedience.
But the story goes even deeper.
Crossing the Jordan was more than a geographic move. It marked the transition from wandering in the wilderness to entering the promised land. It was the boundary between an old season and a new one.
But here is the truth many overlook:
No one carried themselves across.
They followed the Ark.
And that is where the story points beyond Joshua.
Because the Ark symbolized the presence of God, but centuries later, God would do something even greater.
He would come Himself.
Jesus Christ stepped into the brokenness we could never overcome. Where we deserved judgment, He stepped forward. Where sin threatened to drown us, He entered death itself.

At the cross, Jesus took the flood of our sin.
In the resurrection, He opened a way through the impossible.
Jesus is the greater Joshua.
Joshua led Israel across a river.
Jesus leads sinners across sin, death, and the grave.
Because of Him, the greatest barrier between us and God has already been removed.
That is the Gospel.

We are not saved because we were brave enough to step.
We are saved because Christ stepped in first.
Now our obedience flows from grace.

We step not to earn God's love —
we step because we already have it through Jesus.
So if you feel like you are standing at your Jordan today, hear this:
The river in front of you is not stronger than the God who stands with you.

Consecrate your heart.
Trust His presence.
Take the next obedient step.
And when God moves — and He will — everyone around you will see the truth Joshua declared that day:
“By this you shall know that the living God is among you.” — Joshua 3:10
Because someone out there needs to remember:

The river doesn’t decide your future.
God does.
